newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tekala says to buy timber product firms.
newsitem.headline: Tekala says to buy timber product firms.

text.p: Malaysian timber firm Tekala Corp Bhd said it was buying equity stakes in two Sabah state-owned firms involved in timber product manufacturing for 43.16 million ringgit.

Tekala said in a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange that it was buying a 49 percent stake in Pacific Hardwoods Sdn Bhd for 41.3 million ringgit to be paid by issuing new Tekala shares at between 5.20 ringgit and 5.75 ringgit.
It was also buying a 49 percent stake in Cadenza Corp Sdn Bhd for 1.86 million ringgit to be paid by issuing new Tekala shares at between the same price range.
Around 0240 GMT, Tekala stock was down nine cents to 4.96 ringgit.
Both Pacific Hardwoods and Cadenza are currently wholly-owned subsidiaries of Innoprise Corp Sdn Bhd, the investment arm of Sabah-state foundation Yayasan Sabah.
Tekala said Innoprise has accepted the conditional offer pending the signing of a sale and purchase agreement.
Pacific Hardwoods is mainly involved in plywood and sawntimber manufacturing, while Cadenza is involved in timber moulding and manufacturing of blockboard and finger joints.
Both firms operate from their timber complex in Lahad Datu, Sabah.
Pacific Hardwoods has an annual capacity to produce 96,000 cubic metres of plywood and 120,000 cubic metres of sawntimber.
Cadenza's annual capacity is 6,000 cubic metres of moulded timber, 8,400 cubic metres of blockboard and 1,200 cubic metres of finger joints.
Both companies presently obtain their log supplies mainly from Sabah Berjaya Sdn Bhd under a log supply agreement.
